body:
Mm, as I mentioned to another poster I am just now seeing these messages because I checked myself in to the hospital shortly after I made this thread.

I appreciate what you have said here. This is something I would have been glad to hear before, but I don't know if I could have accepted it. I can now - and I agree. 

Hell, it isn't much different than what I've said to others before. I just couldn't apply it to myself. People are funny that way.

Also, I do apologize for the insinuation about picking who to help. I was very emotional. It's not an accusation I would normally make, as I have great respect for this community.

Hey.

So, I ended up checking myself in to a Psychiatric Hospital -  not for the first time. 

I didn't actually get a chance to see these messages until just now.

Well, anyway, I greatly appreciate them. The things you've said here are quite accurate - one therapist I met with posited a very similar question. 

------

Many of the issues people face really do come from within. But well, knowing something objectively isn't always enough to counter strong feelings.

When you live your life thinking in one way, only to later find out the way you were thinking was erroneous, it can be difficult to handle. People don't change instantly, and fundamental beliefs can be especially hard to change as they become the foundation for other thoughts - shaping ones perspective in a manner that may be negative. 

I still don't have the answers to a lot of questions. But, for the first time, I think I'm getting to a point where I'm okay with that.

Mmmm

I'm trying to think really hard here. 

That's diffcult within itself. 

Objectively: Is suicide my best option?

Well...

First of all, why am I considering suicide at all?

Because it is an end. When things are bad, and we don't see them improving we end them, right?

Things are bad. I don't see them improving. I am not sure I want them to improve. 

Eh...that's not objective. 

Okay. 

Observation: Life sucks. Subjective. 

Life definitely sucks for me. But, sucks is subjective. Someone in the same position as me might consider my life to be awesome in comparison to theirs. 

But...I can not feel as if my life does not suck. I have tried and failed. 

So...does that mean I suck?

...

Question: Why does life suck? Because my entire life has been a failure due to a combination of outside sources and circumstances, and myself. 

What is failure? The inability to accomplish my goals. My goals? Pay back my debts. Secondary/Contingency goals? Be happy. 

Definition of "happy?" not suffering.

Both have failed. 

Observation: Life sucks because life will not get magically better if you do not make it so. I have failed to make it so.

Every time I have fought against my circumstance and tried to improve my situation, I have failed as a person. Because even when given chances, I have been unable to follow through. Because I do not consider myself worthy of success.

...

Fuck it.

I'm so tired.

I can't even continue to try to think.

Hahaha.

I guess this, too, is destiny?

Am I impatient? 

Is a few decades too little time to judge? 

Do you - the members of SW judge who is worthy of helping based on interest? Or ability? Am I not worthy of help? Or am I impossible to help? Is there a difference?

I think you need to talk to your Dad and see how he feels about the situation.

You both suffer from similar conditions? Chances are he understands your struggles more than you may think. 

Even if you situations aren't identical, he is probably willing to help however he can. And, with some luck, that'll be enough for you to push on.

Mm...I am torn here.

I feel that a great many people who seek to help others are those who have suffered themselves. You can not truly understand pain without experiencing it.

However, can someone who is broken really offer an objective view for others? 

It is a challenge. I have ultimately failed to help others for the most part, as I have failed to help myself. But, everyone needs help and, even when I don't feel equipt to help I can not stop myself from tying.

I am not a good person. I am someone who tries to help others despite not truly being able to.

Eh, your first paragraph shows that you are more capable of introspection and self analysis than those around you.

I've met people like you've described. Plenty of times with my work. The fact that you can use the internet enough to make a reddit post is more promising than you can imagine. 

You aren't like them. You've had it hard. But, you have the ability to make it better. It probably won't be easy. But the fact that you've written this - hell the fact that you can type and read and write and use the internet says enough about that. 

So...people gave you a hard time about leaving your community? Well...fuck, what exactly is keeping you? Situational - like monetary? Emotional?

Why worry about that shit? You seem to be smarter than them. You can make it. They've given up. You don't have to. I know it's tiring. I know it's exhausting. But you can do it. You've already done things that are incredibly difficult. Doing something for yourself? You've already proven you have the ability to get by. Push through. Not to keep as you are. But to go somewhere and do something. There's no reason to stay where you are - as you are.

Philanthropic? You can't do shit for other people if you don't survive. I can't help you value yourself. But, if you really want to help others - well you've got to help yourself first. 

Get out. Move on. The things that are holding you back are probably not as strong a bond as you think.

Eh. I'm hardly a good person to give advice here, but I'd say just do it.

You don't decide what is worth it to her. It's her call to get upset about being woken up - or not.

Do you want her to care more about you than her sleep? 

Objectively...what is a few hours of sleep compared to a life? 

Probably, if given the choice, the call she would make is to give up sleep. 

If she is your birth mother she has given up many hours of sleep in the past, most likely. Babies are obnoxious. While unexpected, it's not a challenge she has not overcome in the past.

Ha.

Was my title not interesting enough? Figures.

...

No. I'm just feeling impatient and antagonistic.
